translation_en: Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us: Muhammad ibn Ja‘far narrated to us: Shu‘bah narrated to us, saying: I heard ‘Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Qasim say: I heard al-Qasim narrating from ‘Aishah that she wanted to buy Barirah to free her, but they stipulated that her wala’ belong to them. She mentioned this to the Messenger of Allah, who said: “Buy her and free her, for wala’ belongs to the one who frees.” Meat was given to the Messenger of Allah, and they told him it had been given in charity to Barirah. He said: “It is charity for her and a gift for us.” She was given the choice. ‘Abd al-Rahman said that her husband was free. Shu‘bah said: I later asked him about her husband, and he said, “I do not know.”
Ahmad ibn ‘Uthman al-Nawfali narrated it to us: Abu Dawud narrated to us: Shu‘bah narrated to us with this chain, with a report like it.

Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna and Ibn Bashshar narrated it to us, both from Abu Hisham. Ibn al-Muthanna said: Mughirah ibn Salamah al-Makhzumi narrated to us; Abu Hisham said: Wuhaib narrated to us, from ‘Ubayd Allah, from Yazid ibn Ruman, from ‘Urwah, from ‘Aishah, who said: Barirah’s husband was a slave.

Abu al-Tahir narrated to me: Ibn Wahb narrated to us: Malik ibn Anas informed me, from Rabi‘ah ibn Abi ‘Abd al-Rahman, from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, from ‘Aishah, the Prophet’s wife, who said: There were three precedents concerning Barirah: she was given a choice regarding her husband when she was freed; meat was given to her; and the Messenger of Allah came to me while a pot was on the fire. He asked for food, and bread and some household condiments were brought. He asked, “Did I not see a pot on the fire with meat in it?” They said, “Yes, Messenger of Allah, that meat was given in charity to Barirah, and we disliked feeding it to you.” He said, “It is charity for her and a gift from her to us.” The Prophet also said of her: “Wala’ belongs only to the one who frees.”

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah narrated to us: Khalid ibn Makhlad narrated to us, from Sulayman ibn Bilal, from Suhayl ibn Abi Salih, from his father, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: ‘Aishah wanted to buy a slave girl to free her, but her family insisted that wala’ belong to them. She mentioned this to the Messenger of Allah, who said: “Do not let that prevent you, for wala’ belongs to the one who frees.”

Yahya ibn Yahya al-Tamimi informed us: Sulayman ibn Bilal narrated to us, from ‘Abd Allah ibn Dinar, from Ibn ‘Umar, that the Messenger of Allah forbade selling wala’ and giving it as a gift. Muslim said: Everyone relies on ‘Abd Allah ibn Dinar for this hadith.

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah and Zuhayr ibn Harb narrated to us: Ibn ‘Uyaynah narrated to us; Yahya ibn Ayyub, Qutaybah, and Ibn Hujr narrated to us: Isma‘il ibn Ja‘far narrated to us; Ibn Numayr narrated to us: my father narrated to us: Sufyan ibn Sa‘id narrated to us; Ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us: Muhammad ibn Ja‘far narrated to us: Shu‘bah narrated to us; Ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us: ‘Abd al-Wahhab narrated to us: ‘Ubayd Allah narrated to us; and Ibn Rafi‘ narrated to us: Ibn Abi Fudayk narrated to us, from al-Dahhak ibn ‘Uthman. All reported from ‘Abd Allah ibn Dinar, from Ibn ‘Umar, from the Prophet, with a report like it. In the Thaqafi’s report from ‘Ubayd Allah, only selling is mentioned, not gifting.

Muhammad ibn Rafi‘ narrated to me: ‘Abd al-Razzaq informed us: Ibn Jurayj informed us: Abu al-Zubayr informed me that he heard Jabir ibn ‘Abd Allah say: The Prophet assigned each clan its blood-money responsibilities, then wrote: “It is not lawful for a Muslim to claim the alliance of a Muslim man’s freedman without his permission.” I was later informed that he cursed in his document whoever did that.

Qutaybah ibn Sa‘id narrated to us: Ya‘qub, meaning Ibn ‘Abd al-Rahman al-Qari, narrated to us, from Suhayl, from his father, from Abu Hurayrah, that the Messenger of Allah said: “Whoever claims the alliance of a people’s freedman without his patrons’ permission, upon him is the curse of Allah and the angels; neither compensation nor ransom will be accepted from him.”

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah narrated to us: Husayn ibn ‘Ali al-Ju‘fi narrated to us, from Za’idah, from Sulayman, from Abu Salih, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet, who said: “Whoever claims the alliance of a people’s freedman without his patrons’ permission, upon him is the curse of Allah, the angels, and all people. No compensation or ransom will be accepted from him on the Day of Resurrection.” Ibrahim ibn Dinar narrated it to me: ‘Ubayd Allah ibn Musa narrated to us: Shayban narrated to us, from al-A‘mash, with this chain, except that he said: “Whoever allies himself with people other than his patrons without their permission.”

Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna al-‘Anazi narrated to us: Yahya ibn Sa‘id narrated to us, from ‘Abd Allah ibn Sa‘id, Ibn Abi Hind, who narrated to me, from Isma‘il ibn Abi Hakim, from Sa‘id ibn Marjanah, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet, who said: “Whoever frees a believing person, Allah will free from the Fire a limb of his for every limb of that person.”

Dawud ibn Rushayd narrated to us: al-Walid ibn Muslim narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Mutarrif Abu Ghassan al-Madani, from Zayd ibn Aslam, from ‘Ali ibn Husayn, from Sa‘id ibn Marjanah, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Messenger of Allah, who said: “Whoever frees a person, Allah will free from the Fire one of his limbs for every limb of that person, even his private part for that person’s private part.”

Qutaybah ibn Sa‘id narrated to us: Layth narrated to us, from Ibn al-Had, from ‘Umar ibn ‘Ali ibn Husayn, from Sa‘id ibn Marjanah, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: I heard the Messenger of Allah say: “Whoever frees a believing person, Allah will free one limb of him from the Fire for every limb of that person, until He frees his private part for that person’s private part.”

Humayd ibn Mas‘adah narrated to me: Bishr ibn al-Mufaddal narrated to us: ‘Asim, Ibn Muhammad al-‘Umari, narrated to us: Waqid, meaning his brother, narrated to us: Sa‘id ibn Marjanah, the companion of ‘Ali ibn Husayn, narrated to me. He said: I heard Abu Hurayrah say that the Messenger of Allah said: “Any Muslim man who frees a Muslim person, Allah will save one of his limbs from the Fire for every limb of that person.” After hearing this from Abu Hurayrah, I went and told ‘Ali ibn Husayn, who freed a slave of his for whom Ibn Ja‘far had offered him ten thousand dirhams or one thousand dinars.

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah and Zuhayr ibn Harb narrated to us: Jarir narrated to us, from Suhayl, from his father, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah said: “A child cannot repay a parent unless he finds him enslaved, buys him, and frees him.” Ibn Abi Shaybah’s narration says, “his father.”

Abu Kurayb narrated it to us: Waki‘ narrated to us; Ibn Numayr narrated to us: my father narrated to us; and ‘Amr al-Naqid narrated to me: Abu Ahmad al-Zubayri narrated to us. All reported from Sufyan, from Suhayl, with this chain and a report like it; they said, “a child, his father.”
Yahya ibn Yahya al-Tamimi said: I recited to Malik, from Muhammad ibn Yahya ibn Habban, from al-A‘raj, from Abu Hurayrah, that the Messenger of Allah forbade mulamasah and munabadha.
Abu Kurayb and Ibn Abi ‘Umar narrated to us: Waki‘ narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Abu al-Zinad, from al-A‘raj, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet, with a report like it.

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah narrated to us: Ibn Numayr and Abu Usamah narrated to us; Muhammad ibn ‘Abd Allah ibn Numayr narrated to us: my father narrated to us; and Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us: ‘Abd al-Wahhab narrated to us. All reported from ‘Ubayd Allah ibn ‘Umar, from Khubayb ibn ‘Abd al-Rahman, from Hafs ibn ‘Asim, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet, with a report like it.
Qutaybah ibn Sa‘id narrated to us: Ya‘qub, meaning Ibn ‘Abd al-Rahman, narrated to us, from Suhayl ibn Abi Salih, from his father, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet, with a report like it.

Muhammad ibn Rafi‘ narrated to me: ‘Abd al-Razzaq informed us: Ibn Jurayj informed us: ‘Amr ibn Dinar informed me, from ‘Ata’ ibn Mina’, who heard him narrating from Abu Hurayrah, who said: Two kinds of sales were forbidden: mulamasah and munabadha. Mulamasah is when each person touches the other’s garment without examining it. Munabadha is when each throws his garment to the other without either looking at the other’s garment.

Abu al-Tahir and Harmalah ibn Yahya narrated to me—and the wording is Harmalah’s. Ibn Wahb informed us: Yunus informed me, from Ibn Shihab, who informed me that ‘Amir ibn Sa‘d ibn Abi Waqqas said that Abu Sa‘id al-Khudri reported: The Messenger of Allah forbade us two kinds of sales and two kinds of clothing. He forbade mulamasah and munabadha in sales. Mulamasah is when a man touches another’s garment with his hand by night or day and does nothing more than that. Munabadha is when each man throws his garment to the other, and that constitutes their sale without inspection or mutual agreement.
‘Amr al-Naqid narrated it to me: Ya‘qub ibn Ibrahim ibn Sa‘d narrated to us: my father narrated to us, from Salih, from Ibn Shihab, with this chain.

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah narrated to us: ‘Abd Allah ibn Idris, Yahya ibn Sa‘id, and Abu Usamah narrated to us, from ‘Ubayd Allah; and Zuhayr ibn Harb narrated to me—and the wording is his—Yahya ibn Sa‘id narrated to us, from ‘Ubayd Allah, who narrated to me, from Abu al-Zinad, from al-A‘raj, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah forbade pebble sales and sales involving uncertainty.

Yahya ibn Yahya and Muhammad ibn Rumh informed us: al-Layth informed us; Qutaybah ibn Sa‘id narrated to us: Layth narrated to us, from Nafi‘, from ‘Abd Allah, from the Messenger of Allah, that he forbade selling the unborn offspring of an unborn camel.

Zuhayr ibn Harb and Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated to me—and the wording is Zuhayr’s. Yahya, al-Qattan, narrated to us, from ‘Ubayd Allah, who informed me, from Nafi‘, from Ibn ‘Umar, who said: In the pre-Islamic period, people used to trade camel meat deferred until the birth of an unborn camel. The unborn camel means that a she-camel gives birth, then the offspring she has borne becomes pregnant. The Messenger of Allah forbade them from that.

Yahya ibn Ayyub, Qutaybah ibn Sa‘id, and Ibn Hujr narrated to us: Isma‘il, Ibn Ja‘far, narrated to us, from al-‘Ala’, from his father, from Abu Hurayrah, that the Messenger of Allah said: “A Muslim must not outbid his brother’s sale while it is being negotiated.”

Ahmad ibn Ibrahim al-Dawraqi narrated it to me: ‘Abd al-Samad narrated to me: Shu‘bah narrated to us, from al-‘Ala’ and Suhayl, from their fathers, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet; and Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated it to us: ‘Abd al-Samad narrated to us: Shu‘bah narrated to us, from al-A‘mash, from Abu Salih, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet; and ‘Ubayd Allah ibn Mu‘adh narrated to us: my father narrated to us: Shu‘bah narrated to us, from ‘Adi, Ibn Thabit, from Abu Hazim, from Abu Hurayrah, that the Messenger of Allah forbade a man from bidding over his brother’s bid. Al-Dawraqi’s narration says “over his brother’s price.”

Yahya ibn Yahya said: I recited to Malik, from Abu al-Zinad, from al-A‘raj, from Abu Hurayrah, that the Messenger of Allah said: “Do not intercept traders on the road to buy from them; do not sell over one another’s sale; do not bid up prices deceptively; a city-dweller must not sell on behalf of a Bedouin; and do not cause camels or sheep to appear to have more milk than they do. Whoever buys one after that has the choice, after milking it: if satisfied, he keeps it; if displeased, he returns it along with a measure of dates.”

‘Ubayd Allah ibn Mu‘adh al-‘Anbari narrated to us: my father narrated to us: Shu‘bah narrated to us, from ‘Adi, Ibn Thabit, from Abu Hazim, from Abu Hurayrah, that the Messenger of Allah forbade intercepting traders on the road, a city-dweller selling on behalf of a Bedouin, a woman asking for her sister’s divorce, deceptive bidding, falsely inflating the apparent milk yield, and a man bidding over his brother’s bid.
